standard_prerequisites.name: Finite projective dimension for a finite module over a Noetherian ring is equivalent to being perfect
standard_prerequisites.use: Connects the hypothesis to the perfectness language and provides finiteness over R.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Auslander-Buchsbaum formula pd + depth = depth of the ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the three displayed equations whose combination gives additivity.

standard_prerequisites.name: Equality of the depth of a finite module over the ring and over a quotient
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows the three equations to be combined consistently.

core_obligations: Recall that for a finite module, finiteness of projective dimension over R, respectively over R/I, is equivalent to being perfect (proof lines 29872-29874).
Use the cohomology-of-perfect statement to conclude that E has finite projective dimension over R (proof lines 29875-29876).
Apply Auslander-Buchsbaum to obtain the three displayed equations: pd_R(E) + depth(E) = depth(R), pd_{R/I}(E) + depth(E) = depth(R/I), and pd_R(R/I) + depth(R/I) = depth(R) (proof lines 29877-29886).
Observe that the depth of E over R and over R/I agree, as the author notes and as also follows from the depth-goes-down statement (proof lines 29887-29890).
Combine the second and third equations with the first to obtain pd_R(E) = pd_R(R/I) + pd_{R/I}(E), concluding the proof (proof lines 29890-29891).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a Noetherian local ring R, an ideal I, and a nonzero finite module E over R/I, and assumes that R/I has finite projective dimension and that E has finite projective dimension over R/I; it concludes that E has finite projective dimension over R and that pd_R(E) = pd_R(R/I) + pd_{R/I}(E) (source lines 29860-29869). The proof proceeds through the Auslander-Buchsbaum formula. It first recalls that for a finite module, finiteness of projective dimension over R, respectively over R/I, is the same as being perfect (proof lines 29872-29874). It then uses the cohomology-of-perfect statement to conclude that E has finite projective dimension over R (proof lines 29875-29876). The substantive step applies Auslander-Buchsbaum three times, obtaining pd_R(E) + depth(E) = depth(R) with depth taken over R, pd_{R/I}(E) + depth(E) = depth(R/I) with depth taken over R/I, and pd_R(R/I) + depth(R/I) = depth(R) (proof lines 29877-29886). The proof then records that the two depths of E, computed over R and over R/I respectively, agree — a fact the author calls trivial and which also follows from the depth-goes-down statement (proof lines 29887-29890). Adding the second and third equations and comparing with the first yields the stated additivity (proof lines 29890-29891). The non-routine content is the correct bookkeeping of which depth is being used in each Auslander-Buchsbaum instance.
